text:
I usually don’t like to complain. But after my wife’s feedback(also a very negative experience), I feel like I have to say something.

First of all: the service
The whole procedure was painful. Very painful, and more painful than usual. (I have went to at least 5-10 different clinics before, this was the most painful experience.)

The sense I got was that the doctor didn’t place any care into his craft, and was going along without a care of the patient’s pain. Almost felt like he was sadistic in ‘wanting to cause pain’ in the patient.

I didn’t feel doctor being careful, or caring for the patient, more like intending to inflict pain. (Even my experience with newly graduated practicing dentists of huachiew uni. was much better than this—this is a sign of an attitude and caring problem)

There was no communication with the patient or warning that “this part may hurt” or anything, just inflicting pain in just scaling the teeth.

Second: Attitude
I’m not sure where this doctor learned his manners or how he grew up. After sitting down for less than 2 minutes, the doctor mentioned to his nurse “I thought I told the counter not to accept Chinese people.”

First of all I am Taiwanese, and have been living in Thailand for over 20 years. There was so much wrong with this comment, showing racism, as well as deep disregard of manners/respect as it was said right in front of my face, and it was clear I understood Thai.

There was so much wrong, and negative on this visit, I feel it must be made known to the public, the ‘slightly overweight’ dentist with glasses.

1. Your craft is not acceptable
2. Your attitude and sentiment toward “Chinese people”
3. Your manners, culture, and upbringing.

This sort of behavior and Unprofessionalism should not be tolerated. And must be made known to the public.
